conventions.convention: Assume AC, T>0, finite positive state and Brownian dimensions, a complete usual filtered probability space, and Brownian increments independent of the preceding sigma-algebra. Local coefficients are jointly Borel, bounded on compact subsets, and locally Lipschitz in state uniformly in time.
The compact exhaustion is K_n={x∈U: |x|≤n, dist(x,Uᶜ)≥1/n}; distance to the empty complement is +∞. Exit is from int K_n, capped at T; empty early exhaustion sets give exit time zero.
Tamed Euler uses b_h(x)=b(x)/(1+h|b(x)|), h=T/N≤1, left-endpoint diffusion, and the continuous adapted interpolation specified by the algorithm.

Drift-implicit Euler uses Y_{n+1}=R_h(Y_n+σ(Y_n)ΔW_n), with full-space global dissipativity and μ≥0. Its interpolation is a pathwise continuous extension. Failed root certification returns solve-failure without assigning the next state.

CIR parameters κ,θ,σ are strictly positive and satisfy the inclusive Feller condition 2κθ≥σ². The numerical Lamperti input may be zero; the exact positive-solution and convergence theorems start from deterministic x₀>0.

The tamed theorem estimates the continuous path supremum in L²; the drift-implicit theorem estimates the maximum over grid points in L²; the CIR theorem asserts grid-maximum convergence in probability without an Lp rate.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC and the filtered Brownian and initial-state hypotheses of the local SDE definition on U=Rᵈ. For autonomous C¹ drift b satisfying ⟨x−y,b(x)−b(y)⟩≤L|x−y|² and ||Db(x)||≤C(1+|x|^q), globally Lipschitz diffusion, and all finite initial moments, the maximal local strong solution is global on [0,T], unique up to indistinguishability, and E sup_{0≤t≤T}|X_t|^p<∞ for every finite p≥1.

Assume AC and the usual filtered Brownian conventions. For predictable d×m matrix G and real p≥2 with E(∫₀ᵀ||G_s||_F² ds)^(p/2)<∞, the continuous vector Itô integral satisfies E sup_{0≤t≤T}|∫₀ᵗG_s dW_s|^p≤C_{p,d} E(∫₀ᵀ||G_s||_F² ds)^(p/2), with C_{p,d} independent of G and T.

Under the data of the local SDE definition, with E|ξ|²<∞, a local strong solution up to exit from U exists on the given filtered space and is unique up to indistinguishability before its maximal lifetime ζ=lim_n τ_n. Its stopped solutions form the compatible family specified in that definition; ζ=T is not asserted.

Assume AC and the coefficient, Brownian, and initial-moment hypotheses of thm-superlinear-sde-global-existence-and-moments. For N≥max(1,ceil T), h=T/N, and tamed Euler grid values, sup_N max_{0≤n≤N} E|Y_n|^p<∞ for every finite p≥1.

For κ,θ,σ>0 with 2κθ≥σ² and a=(4κθ−σ²)/8, a positive local CIR solution has Z=√X satisfying dZ=(a/Z−κZ/2)dt+(σ/2)dW up to every compact exit time. For every h>0, z≥0, and real ΔW, the corresponding drift-implicit Lamperti equation has exactly one positive root, equal to the algorithm's displayed root.

Assume AC, the local filtered Brownian conventions, κ,θ,σ>0, deterministic x₀>0, and 2κθ≥σ². The CIR SDE has a unique global strong solution on every finite horizon; its paths remain strictly positive and finite, and sup_{0≤t≤T} E X_t^p<∞ for every finite p≥1.

concerns.concern: Steps 1.2 and 2.2 use martingale and finite-energy maximal inequalities for integrands involving Y_n, but the proof never first establishes finite moments of the numerical iterates. In particular, step 2.2 calls M_j a martingale and applies the published L¹ maximal bound, whose Statement requires finite expected quadratic energy. This closes immediately for each fixed N: the Lipschitz resolvent gives |R_h(u)|≤|R_h(0)|+|u|, and linear growth of σ, Gaussian increments, and the all-moment initial assumption give all finite moments of Y_n by finite induction. Combined with the exact-solution moments, this licenses the integrals and finite v_j used in the recurrence. The argument should make this prerequisite explicit.

seams_checked.note: This is preparatory comparison context. The supplier's local-to-global RMS lemma requires a Lipschitz drift-error recurrence, O(h²) predictable defect, and O(h³) centered-defect second moment to conclude order one. Neither owned half-order proof invokes that lemma or transfers its conclusion; both supply independent moment and martingale recurrences.

The actual supplier thm-backward-euler-dissipative-resolvent-contraction assumes continuous full-space drift and global dissipativity with μ≥0, yielding a globally defined inverse with factor (1+hμ)⁻¹. Taking f(t,x)=b(x) satisfies its hypotheses in both owned consumers. The page and algorithms preserve the distinction between exact resolvent existence and finite solve certification; no stochastic contraction is inferred merely from deterministic contraction.
